  • Sacha Arnoud

    12K followers

    Big news for Meta Neural Band owners! 🎉 Starting this week, we're rolling out a groundbreaking new way to message: writing with your finger on any surface (https://lnkd.in/g6t_9sPC). Imagine messaging as simply as you wrote in elementary school—no keyboards, no accessories, just you and the neural band. This isn't just a new feature; it's a fundamental step in the evolution of human-computer interaction. The neural band natively understands written text using human biology (EMG at the wrist), eliminating the need for users to learn a new interface (physical/virtual keyboards, touch screen UIs or mice). This is a new step in the paradigm shift from humans adapting to computers to computers communicating like humans. While much of the recent AI focus has been on language models and reasoning, the same underlying techniques have been taking perceptive AI to quite a mature level over the last 10 years. First it revolutionized computer vision (https://lnkd.in/gejhZ9Vu) and speech recognition (ASR, TTS). Beyond human senses, it enabled the processing of complex sensor suites that made applications like self driving cars possible (https://lnkd.in/ghxE2hvR). When we launched the Neural Band last fall (https://lnkd.in/gyuzRVeD), we proved for the first time that a consumer-grade device could accurately capture and process neural activations. Initial gestures were innovative, but handwriting is different. While finger differentiated taps and swipes could have arguably been implemented using other modalities, the richness and accuracy of the signal required for handwriting requires the high-information-entropy bandwidth unique to an EMG-based device. I can't wait for many of you to experience the "waouh, this is new!" feeling for yourself. While this is the culmination of 10 years of research (https://lnkd.in/gxm_gc3z), we're just getting started! Stay tuned for the even more exciting, next-level capabilities we are working on. #MetaNeuralBand #HumanComputerInteraction #PerceptiveAI #Innovation #EMG

  • Phil Bogle

    Databricks • 1K followers

    Update on new Listify features, and experiments with Wap and ChatGPT 5: Warp is running a $5 ChatGPT promotion (https://www.warp.dev/), integrated with their Agentic terminal/dev environment. I've been using Gemini Pro and the Gemini CLI so far to build Listify (https://lnkd.in/gmU5YdUE), my hobbyist AI+flutter powered list management app, but thought I'd give ChatGPT 5 a chance for comparisons sake and to see how smoothly the LLMs could hand off the codebase. Observations: - Handoff was seamless, GPT5 had no problems understanding the code base and working with it. - I really didn't see a big difference in coding capabilities between GPT 5 and Gemini Pro 2.5, but it's true this is not an extremely challenging app. - GPT5 has much better testing discipline than Gemini Pro; it suggested adding a number of tests whereas Gemini never even considered to offer. - The Warp terminal is definitely better than Gemini CLI due to the greater power that Warp offers; e.g. formatting is richer, you can upload images and easily specify files as context, and the collapsible sections provide a better experience for looking at diffs and log output. - I am still uncertain if the agentic environment of the future will look more like a browser, an IDE, or a terminal. Toggling back and forth between terminal mode and agentic mode in Warp is awkward. While you can give commands like "git push" to the LLM instead of the shell, it is terribly slow to respond. Since I last wrote, I've added the following features: - an AI-powered autosort and group feature. For example, if you have a shopping list, it will be break it into labeled sections like "produce", "dairy", "snacks", where each section contains things that are likely to be nearby in the store. This makes shopping faster. - an "Export to Google Tasks" feature to the app for people who like tahe scanning/parsing features of Listify but want to live in Google Tasks. (The backend but not UI integration was done so let GPT5 take over the UI. - more optimistic updates to make the UI feel snappier. - I also added a feature that lets you add a section header by long pressing on add item. Obigatory plug: Please LMK if you'd like to be a tester for the Android version of Listify, I still need to get to 12 testers to get it listed on the main app store for convenience of download. The web link above gives you an idea of the feature set but the mobile experience is much better. I still also need to get the iOS version up but haven't jumped through all the certifcate hoops.
